data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's mechanism only addresses administrative/human (configuration, deployment) correlated failures and treats independent operators using different schedules/tools as sufficient to eliminate them. But the problem explicitly requires distinguishing failures that are TRULY independent from failures that merely APPEAR uncorrelated until a shared cause is found. The mechanism provides no causal basis for asserting operator independence is genuine rather than apparent: independent operators can independently converge on the same flawed configuration (same industry defaults, same upstream library bug, same TLS or DNS setting) without any shared deployment platform or central registry, producing a correlated outage that the given counterconditions do not catch. The counterconditions are limited to a shared managed service or shared config/registry, so they fail to screen common-cause convergence that arises through homogeneous knowledge rather than shared infrastructure. Thus the causal claim outstrips the evidence-distinguishing mechanism the problem demands.
